script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for December 21. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Every morning, something pulls you from sleep.  For some, it's obligation.  For others, it's excitement.

In Okinawa, Japan, there's no word for retirement—because the concept of ikigai means you always have a reason to get up. This intersection of what you love, what you're good at, what the world needs, and what you can be paid for creates lasting motivation. Research consistently links purpose to physical health.  People with a strong sense of why live longer, have lower rates of heart disease, and recover faster from setbacks.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You don't need to have it all figured out.  You just need something worth getting up for tomorrow.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Purpose Clarity - The Why Question.

Here's your activity: Write one sentence that completes this: 'Tomorrow, I'm getting up because...' Make it specific and personal. Post it where you'll see it in the morning. This helps you articulate a simple, personal reason for getting up each day.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why you get up can be applied to purpose clarity - the why question. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
